producer: hand-curated 2026-09-29 (one row per pattern -> industry); consumed by src/agentic/fetch_pib_releases.py at consolidation
purpose: transparent map from government-policy terms in PIB press releases to OUR industry names, producing pib_releases.industries_tagged

taxonomy.source: data/derived/screener_industry.parquet column industry (screener.in / NSE basic industry, HTML-unescaped)
taxonomy.validation: fetch_pib_releases.load_industry_keywords() raises if any industry string is not in that column

columns.pattern: Python regex, applied case-insensitively and wrapped in \b(?: ... )\b
columns.industry: exact industry string from our taxonomy (note 'Telecom -  Equipment & Accessories' has two spaces, 'Road AssetsToll, Annuity, Hybrid-Annuity' has none)
columns.ministry_regex: optional; the row only applies when the release's ministry matches (used for Ministry of Defence procurement language)
columns.note: why the link is direct, and abbreviations deliberately left out

matching_rules: text = release title, then the first 600 characters of body_text (body only exists when body_fetched is True)

ministry / minister / department NAME phrases ('Ministry of Coal', 'Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying', 'Coal Ministry') are removed before matching, so a ministry's own name never tags its industry
each industry is tagged at most once per release; evidence is kept in pib_releases.industry_tag_evidence as '<industry><=<matched text>@title|lead'

excluded_on_review.DRI: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, not direct-reduced iron
excluded_on_review.bare 'highway', 'airport', 'spectrum', ': route/location/idiom/office clean-up/cultural uses dominated a 2026-09 sample

limitations: keyword heuristic, not labels: expect false positives (e.g. a route along an expressway) and misses (policy described without these terms)
only direct links: second-order effects (e.g. steel demand from rail capex) are deliberately not tagged
PLI schemes are tagged through the sector noun in the same text ('PLI for bulk drugs' -> Pharmaceuticals), not a separate PLI rule
EMS makers Kaynes/Syrma sit in 'Industrial Products' in our taxonomy, which is too broad to tag from semiconductor/electronics terms
